title: Date Labelling & Stock Rotation (FIFO)
blurb: How date labels and First In, First Out rotation keep food safe, cut waste and avoid serving out-of-date stock.
siteNotes: The venue's labelling system and what must go on a label
Where and how discarded food is recorded
Who the supervisor is on each shift
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-36 (the venue's 10-minute trainer). Taught as written.

CHECK: the trainer says serving food past its use-by date is "breaking the law". This is broadly correct (food past its use-by is treated as unsafe and must not be sold), but confirm you are happy with the wording.
Shelf life once opened or prepared is set by the venue's own food safety management system, not by the trainer, which only says to label with the date. Check the venue's own rules are in siteNotes.

cards.title: Date Labelling & Stock Rotation (FIFO)
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- rotate stock using FIFO
- tell a use-by from a best-before date
- label, check and throw out stock correctly

cards.title: More than saving money
cards.body: Good stock control saves money, but it is also a food safety essential. Serve something past its use-by date and you could make a guest seriously ill, as well as breaking the law. Two simple habits keep us safe.

items.title: Date labelling
items.text: Everyone can see how fresh it is.

cards.title: First In, First Out
cards.body: FIFO is the golden rule of rotation. When you put a delivery away, place the newer stock BEHIND the older stock. The older items get used first and nothing gets lost at the back until it has gone off. It is a tiny habit that dramatically cuts both waste and risk.

items.title: Old forward
items.text: Older items go to the front.

items.title: New behind
items.text: Newer stock goes behind the older.

items.title: Oldest first
items.text: Nothing is lost at the back.

cards.title: Use-by or best-before
cards.body: Know your dates. They do not mean the same thing.

left.title: Best-before
items: May be past its best but is generally still safe

right.title: Use-by
items: Never use or serve after it, full stop

cards.title: Date it when you open it
cards.body: When you open or prepare something, label it with the date so everyone knows how fresh it is and when it needs using.

cards.title: When in doubt, throw it out
cards.body: Check dates as part of your routine and remove anything that is out of date or looks unfit, recording what you have thrown away. If you are ever unsure whether something is still good, do not gamble with a guest's health. Throw it out and tell your supervisor.

items.title: Check dates
items.text: Make it part of your routine.

items.title: Remove
items.text: Anything out of date or unfit.

items.title: Record
items.text: Write down what you threw away.

items.title: Tell
items.text: If unsure, throw it out and tell your supervisor.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- FIFO: newer stock goes behind older stock
- Use-by is safety. Never serve after it
- Best-before is quality
- Label with the date when you open or prepare
- When in doubt, throw it out and tell your supervisor

cards.why: FIFO is First In, First Out, the golden rule of rotation.

cards.q: When putting a delivery away, newer stock goes…
cards.why: Put newer stock behind older stock so the older items are used first.

cards.q: A "use-by" date is about food safety.
cards.why: Use-by is about SAFETY. Never use or serve food after its use-by date.
Best-before is about QUALITY. The food may be past its best but is generally still safe.

cards.q: It is fine to serve food a day or two after its use-by date.
cards.why: Never use or serve food after its use-by date, full stop.

cards.q: What should you do when you open or prepare an item?
cards.why: Label it with the date so everyone knows how fresh it is and when it needs using.

cards.q: Good stock rotation cuts both waste and food-safety risk.
cards.why: FIFO is a tiny habit that dramatically cuts both waste and risk.

cards.q: You are unsure whether something is still good. You should…
options: Serve it anyway and hope for the best
Sell it cheap at the bar or pass
Taste a little to check it is fine
Throw it out and tell a supervisor
cards.why: When in doubt, throw it out. Do not gamble with a guest's health.

cards.q: You should record food that you throw away.
cards.why: Remove anything out of date or unfit, recording what you have thrown away.

cards.q: Why place older stock at the front?
options: So it gets used first and nothing goes off at the back
So the shelves look tidy for deliveries
So newer stock stays cooler at the back
So it is easier to count
cards.why: Older stock at the front is used first, so nothing is lost at the back until it has gone off.
